title: Cross-Leads Acceleration Brief - June 22 2027
content:
Attendees: Priya Shah (chair), Marcus Liu, Aisha Banerjee, Diego Alvarez, Rina Kapoor, Elena Novak (SRE), Tom Hsu (Solutions)

Purpose: Quick cross-team alignment on acceleration workstreams that need leadership decisions or resource shifts this sprint. Focus: capacity experiments, high-risk rollouts, and one customer-impact item.

1) Quick pulse (1-2 mins per lead)
- Platform infra: running the new continuous-batching prototype on a small pool; 8% median latency improvement in p95 under synthetic workload; CPU utilization slightly higher than expected on control plane tasks.
- Serving runtime: kernel selection refactor landing in canary; observed a 12% token-cost reduction for MPT-30B quantized path in early tests.
- Private deployments: pilot install on customer A (regulated fintech) delayed by VPN cert rotation; on-prem team needs one extra engineer for next two weeks.
- Observability: trace ingestion backlog reduced after Kafka tuning; a recurring spike at 03:00 UTC still unexplained.
- Solutions/SE: two enterprise customers flagged SLA questions for Dedicated — want throughput guarantees for scheduled batch jobs.

2) Customer incident readout (15 mins)
- Incident: Customer B saw intermittent 5–10s tail-latency spikes when KV cache warmed on long-context requests (customer dataset length ~12k tokens). Root cause suspected: cache eviction + disk-backed checkpointing fallback triggered during batch consolidation window.
- Impact: degraded UX for production scoring pipeline; no data leak; 6 total requests affected across a 48-hour window.
- Short-term mitigation: disable disk fallback for that cluster; bump cache capacity using reserve quota (Marcus to apply today).
- Long-term: Serving runtime to add a lightweight async checkpoint flow + proactive cache pre-warming hook for scheduled long-context jobs (owner: Diego, target: 2 sprints).
- Action: INF-1289 created to track, priority P1 for affected customer. Linked artifact above.

3) Capacity experiment decision (10 mins)
- Proposal recap: test ephemeral dedicated pools that auto-scale from host spot GPUs for low-cost burst capacity; expected cost delta: -18% for spiky workloads but higher cold-start risk.
- Risk heatmap discussed: security/tenancy isolation (medium), cold-starts for 2–5s (high for latency-sensitive customers), billing complexity (low).
- Decision: greenlight 6-week experiment limited to non-SLA customers and opt-in Dedicated customers; telemetry gating and kill-switch required. Rina to draft experiment playbook and rollout checklist by EOD Friday.
- Action items: create metric dashboard (observability), add customer opt-in flow (console), legal to review billing TOS addendum.

4) Rollout gating for kernel-selection refactor (8 mins)
- Observations: canary shows memory footprint variance on larger sequence lengths. Need two extra memory-profiling testcases from research (Priya to coordinate).
- Gate criteria proposed: no >5% p99 regression on any production traffic slice; automated rollback configured; canary window increased to 72 hours for heavy sequences.
- Decision: hold broad rollout until profiling tests complete (target +1 week). Marcus to publish list of test slices and owners.

5) Cross-team dependencies & headcount asks (5 mins)
- Private deployments requested 1 FTE from infra for two weeks (onboarding and VPN certificate fix). Approval granted from platform leads; Marcus to OK resource plan.
- Observability needs a small infra task force (2 engineers) to finish Kafka tuning and trace pipeline changes. Elena to propose names.

6) Open issues / blockers (rapid-fire)
- SLO drift: console shows drift for embeddings latency in eu-west-1 during 02:00–04:00 UTC. Hypothesis: nightly batch maintenance jobs. Action: product-ops to surface schedule; infra to temporarily shift maintenance window.
- Eval regression alert: Redwood Optimize flagged a small but consistent decline in BLEU for recent MPT-level fine-tune; Research lead to triage.
- Security audit: Private deployment checklist requires HSM integration sign-off; legal/compliance engaged.

7) Action items (owner -> due)
- Marcus Liu -> apply cache reserve to affected cluster (today)
- Diego Alvarez -> design async checkpoint + pre-warm hook (end of sprint)
- Rina Kapoor -> experiment playbook and rollback criteria for ephemeral pools (Fri EOD)
- Priya Shah -> coordinate memory-profiling testcases with research (3 business days)
- Elena Novak -> propose names for Kafka/trace task force (Mon)
- Tom Hsu -> prepare customer comms template for opt-in burst pools (Tue)

8) Notes-to-self / unresolved questions
- Need clearer billing language for burst capacity; should be simple and predictable for customers doing committed Dedicated + bursts.
- How do we communicate the p95/p99 change windows without alarming customers? Consider a per-route status indicator in console.
- Follow-up: schedule 30-min deep-dive next Tue for kernel selection memory profile with runtime + research + infra.

9) Quick wins for next week (targets)
- Turn on increased canary window and add automated p99 regression alert for kernel refactor.
- Patch KV-cache fallback to be non-blocking on disk writes.
- Draft customer-facing FAQ for ephemeral pools.

Minutes submitted by: Priya Shah

Raw scratch notes:
- "should we allow customers to set per-model cold-start tolerances?" — idea floated by Tom
- Slack thread: #platform-weekly -> referenced there are some logs when trace backlog spikes
- Linear tickets to create: platform-burst-experiment, kernel-profile-suite, kv-cache-async

Next meeting: Tue 2027-06-29 09:30 PT (30 mins)
